source.title: Probing Large Language Model Hidden States for Adverse Drug Reaction Knowledge
source.authors: J. Berkowitz; D. Weissenbacher; A. Srinivasan; N. Friedrich; J. M. Acitores Cortina; S. Kivelson; G. G. Hernandez; N. Tatonetti

record.tranche_reason: The study compares ADR classification performance using SAE-derived features with performance using unaltered activations, and reports no significant difference. This challenges V5's prediction of a meaningful loss in task-relevant information, though it does not directly test whether retaining the SAE error term changes results.
record.gate_note: The study uses Gemma Scope SAEs and compares downstream ADR classification using SAE features against classifiers on raw activations. It does not measure SAE reconstruction errors, error predictability or scaling, token overlap across SAE sizes, or the effects of adding or removing an error term. Its standalone SAE AUC results and comparisons with generative prompting do not test those error claims.
record.test_reason: The study uses Gemma Scope SAE latents as probe inputs for ADR classification and reports its own pipeline's AUCs. It never removes, keeps or measures an SAE error term. It does not run circuits or steering, and it does not measure model behaviour or loss under reconstruction. The SAE-versus-raw comparison is linear-probe accuracy on pooled latents, not loss of model function. That is a related but different construct, so it does not test V5 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that SAE features probe as well as raw activations, with no significant difference. They state this suggests 'information lost in reconstruction is minimal' and that SAEs simplify the task without losing critical information. This is an interpretation: they never measure reconstruction error or the error term.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares downstream ADR classification from SAE features and raw activations; it does not reproduce the original study's measurements of SAE reconstruction error or its scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: The comparison spans SAE layers 9, 20, and 31 and raw-activation classifiers across residual blocks; the text reports no significant overall performance difference.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes on Gemma Scope SAE latents (layers 9/20/31, Gemma-2-9b-it) reached ADR classification AUCs of 0.90–0.96. The authors report these as not significantly different (p > 0.05) from MLP probes on raw residual activations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents retain enough task-relevant information for downstream linear probing to match raw-activation probes on a small biomedical fact-classification task.

record.problems: The comparison is on one model and one downstream task. The text gives no exact AUC values for the SAE-versus-raw comparison, and the claim about retained task information does not directly establish anything about the SAE error term.
record.rows_left_out: Standalone SAE classification AUCs, SAE-versus-generation comparisons, and feature annotations were left out because they do not measure SAE error or test the retention comparison relevant to V5.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of SAE error from input activations.
Per-token error-norm predictability, shared failure contexts across SAE sizes, persistence with scale.
Loss harm from splicing in SAE reconstructions vs same-norm random errors.
Split of error into linear (unlearned features) and nonlinear parts.
Effect of keeping or dropping the error term on circuits, steering or model behaviour.
Whether dark matter reflects SAE training choices or shrinks with better architectures or objectives.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V5 'challenges' label should be dropped. Probe accuracy on SAE latents does not address whether the SAE error term carries model function. The 'no significant difference' claim has no described test, effect size or numbers in the text; it appears only in the abstract, the Discussion and Figure 3. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, overlap in contexts where different sizes fail, and error persistence with scale.
Whether replacing activations with SAE reconstructions harms model loss more than same-sized random errors.
Whether linear error contains unlearned features and nonlinear error resists further dictionary learning.
The study tests ADR classification from SAE features against raw-activation classifiers, but does not test circuits, steering, or whether explicitly retaining the SAE error term changes behavior.
Whether training choices or alternative architectures cause dark matter, or whether it shrinks with improved architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9b-it
rows.size_stated: 9b parameters; raw activations: 3584 dimensions; SAE: 131,072 dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Compared ADR classification performance using SAE-derived features with performance using unaltered activations.

conditions.value: acute kidney injury, acute liver injury, acute myocardial infarction, and gastrointestinal bleeds

rows.baseline: Neural networks trained on unaltered model activations
rows.value: Linear classifiers on SAE outputs; the study reports no significant performance differences (p > 0.05).
rows.note: The comparison is reported as a general result across the tested layers and outcomes; exact comparison AUC values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The row compares downstream probe AUC (L1 logistic regression on SAE latents vs a 10-unit MLP on raw residuals). It does not measure model behaviour lost when the SAE error term is dropped, so it does not bear on V5. The two probes also differ in architecture, not just in input. Raw MLPs span all layers while the SAEs cover only 9, 20 and 31. No comparison AUCs or test procedure are reported, only 'no significant differences (p > 0.05)'. With 399 test cases, power is limited. Treat as the study's own method compared with a baseline, not a test row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-9b-it ADR classification using the tested SAE layers and raw-activation classifiers
reader_labels.reason: The study reports no significant AUC difference between SAE-feature and raw-activation classifiers, rather than a meaningful loss in ADR classification performance; this rests on r1.
